source.title: Symphony No. 9, Op. 95 — I. Adagio — Allegro molto

patches.basis: The legacy trCueWhile wrapper passes mc to transposedCueDuring, whose modern argument is a pitch rather than a NoteEvent. Change only that declared parameter type; retain all supplied pitches, cue music and source notes. The driver must establish compiled/published pitch-onset multiset identity.

transposeRanges.basis: E trumpet sounds a major third above written pitch, not the horn's minor sixth below (https://utminers.utep.edu/charlesl/transpose.html). Original score IMSLP405834 PDF7/printed185, bar19, writes D5/E4; source transposition e gives F#4/G#3 instead of F#5/G#4. Correct until the C-trumpet declaration at bar149/source q342; C uses c' and needs no change.

Same E-trumpet octave correction after source brass.notesA.ily returns to transposition e at bar285/source q614; stop at transposition c' at bar396/source q836. These bounds follow the conductor's numbered bars and instrument-change declarations, not audio detector results.

bars.description: Written bars 1–176, then 181–452: no exposition repeat; first ending 177–180 omitted. Independent local source/audio feature comparison over the closing theme and junction supports the second ending into the G–B–D-sharp development, not a return to the E-minor Allegro. The selected traversal has mean chroma cosine 0.858088, versus 0.707302 for the first ending plus exposition repeat and 0.834374 for both endings without repeating; fresh pitch-energy overlays were inspected. These are local order diagnostics, not an accepted full alignment. Bars 1–23 retain the encoder's doubled Adagio durations (4/4 rather than original 4/8), then 2/4 from bar 24. Canonical extent: 452 bars/950 quarters; selected performed extent: 448 bars/942 quarters.

endpoints.basis: Independent pitch-energy inspection, not listening: opening E3–G3–E4 begins near 0.8 s (rise peak 0.84); the stronger 2.58 s rise is a later swell, not the first attack. The final separated E-minor chord begins at 602.20 s (first coherent rise peak 602.24), with staggered upper-part energy around 602.36; the broad 596–603 window would select an earlier chord at 598.32. The final pitch set is MIDI 40,52,55,59,64,67,71,76,79,83,88. Windows derive from source chord/order and fresh energy plots, not detector thresholds. Production alignment remains withheld upstream on immutable-source multiset correspondence.

provenance: The original published MIDI is canonical, not an already repeated performance: every sounding track ends at source q948.5 within the 950-quarter, 452-bar source. The conductor alone carries the exposition volta; named instrumental variables contain the written first and second endings once. String unfoldRepeats expands written tremolos, not an exposition repeat.

Published MIDI track 5 (trombone:) has an unmatched E3/MIDI52 note-off at q856. Regenerate the named source staves with LilyPond 2.24.4, retaining the original MIDI grouping, and require aggregate pitch/onset multiset equality against the immutable published MIDI before sounding-pitch corrections and recorded bar order. No malformed MIDI message is silently suppressed and no source part is invented.

Current source-proof blocker: the immutable MIDI contains 11,809 note-on messages, modern source compilation 11,808. The sole multiset difference is one extra published E3/MIDI52 attack at source q855.5 (bar405, quarter offset1.5), in a zero-time on/off/on sequence followed by an unmatched duplicate off at q856. The modern file has a normal single attack there and no other pitch/onset differences. The mandatory multiset gate is retained; no artificial duplicate note, zero duration, discarded MIDI message or weakened comparison is introduced to force acceptance.

Generated MIDI omits key-signature metadata through Staff Key_performer removal: a transposed source key otherwise emits the non-standard eight-sharp MIDI key rejected by mido. Printed key signatures, sounding note events, source durations and instrumental transpositions remain unchanged; the required published pitch/onset multiset comparison remains active.

A clarinets, E horns I/II, C-to-E horns III/IV, flute II's brief piccolo change (c'' then c'), and double bass bass_8 retain source sounding transpositions. Only E-trumpet sections receive the documented regional +12 correction; C-trumpet sections already use c' and stay unchanged. Original score IMSLP405834 PDF5/printed183 shows opening bass written E4, sounding E3/MIDI52, while cello sounds E4/MIDI64. No blanket bass octave lowering. Other parts are non-transposing; identities follow source variables, not MIDI patches.
All timing remains provisional and has not been checked by ear. Source duration warping is not a measured release or a transcription of tremolo/articulation performance.
